title: Experimental Characterization of a Compact Gyroid-Pipe Heat Exchanger for Fuel Cell Powered Electric Aircraft Propulsion
publisher: Engineering Proceedings (MDPI), 15th EASN Conference; DLR repository copy
summary: DLR's Institute of Electrified Aero Engines in Cottbus designed, printed and tested three variants of a compact TPMS gyroid-pipe heat exchanger with embedded coolant channels for fuel-cell aircraft, and compared it with a conventional louvered-fin plate heat exchanger. The best case transferred 6.2 kW on the coolant side, and one variant reached a gravimetric power density of 1.59 kW/kg, against a 10 kW/kg target the authors cite. The louvered-fin design outperformed the gyroid-pipe design overall, mainly because of the gyroid's higher pressure loss, though the gyroid had higher volumetric and gravimetric power density. Stretching the TPMS curvature along the air path improved both heat transfer and pressure loss.
thermal: Air-coolant radiator for fuel-cell aircraft propulsion.
manufacturing: Gyroid-pipe cores made by additive manufacturing and tested over a range of flows and temperatures.

title: Optimization of a Lightweight Gyroid-Based Heat Exchanger for Space Applications
publisher: ICFFTS 2025 proceedings (International ASET); Politecnico di Torino repository
summary: Politecnico di Torino, Thales Alenia Space Italia and the CIM4.0 competence centre designed and metal-printed a compact sheet-gyroid heat exchanger for the active thermal control system of crewed space modules. They built two modular prototypes of nine counter-flow modules each: the first validated the modular concept and thermal design, the second an optimised design of the manifolds and connections between modules. Tests using the effectiveness-NTU method showed performance consistent with an ideal counter-flow exchanger.
thermal: Compact liquid heat exchanger for crewed-module thermal control.
manufacturing: Metal additive manufacturing of gyroid modules and printed manifolds; measured with effectiveness-NTU tests.

title: Design and Fabrication of a C-Shaped Oscillating Heat Pipe with Integrated Heat Sink via Laser Powder Bed Fusion
summary: University of Missouri researchers designed a C-shaped oscillating heat pipe that joins several conventional layouts into one continuous loop, with a water-block heat sink built on top, and printed it by laser powder bed fusion. The design included features for getting powder out of the internal channels. The prototype was checked for channel formation, de-powdering and structural fidelity by inspection and basic operation; performance optimisation is still under way.
thermal: Passive two-phase heat spreading with an integrated liquid heat sink.
manufacturing: Laser powder bed fusion with designed-in de-powdering routes.

title: AMC (Additive Manufacturing for Cubesats)
summary: The AMC project plans pulsating heat pipes built into the structure of a CubeSat, so one printed part carries both load and heat. Argotec leads requirements, design and assembly, integration and test, and Prima Industrie will print and characterise the samples and heat pipe. No figures or dates are given.
thermal: Pulsating heat pipes moving heat across a small satellite's structure.

title: NATHENA - New Additive manufacTuring Heat ExchaNger for Aeronautic
summary: NATHENA was an EU Clean Sky 2 project (March 2018 to November 2022, €1.5m) to design compact air-air heat exchangers made by additive manufacturing for hybrid propulsion, in aluminium for low temperatures and Inconel for high. It used multiphysics simulation of lattice and thin-walled structures with topological and parametric optimisation, checked by sample tests. Targets were 0.5 to 500 kW, 200-400 °C temperature difference and at most 100 mbar pressure drop; TRIMIS lists no results.
thermal: Compact air-air heat exchangers for hybrid-electric propulsion.
manufacturing: Printed lattice and thin-wall cores in aluminium and Inconel, optimised by simulation.

title: Exclusive: Inside the secrets of F1's new driver cooling kit
summary: Chillout Motorsports adapted its Cypher Pro Micro Cooler for Formula 1 at the FIA's request: a box with a micro-compressor, evaporator and condenser feeding about 48 m of tubing in a fireproof shirt. The system weighs just under 2 kg plus about 300 g of mesh, and the FIA allows a 5 kg minimum-weight increase; the FIA can require it above 30.5 °C. No measured effectiveness data.
manufacturing: Miniaturised cooling unit in a carbon-fibre housing; bespoke flame-resistant tubing.
gate_reason: Driver-comfort cooling kit: thermal, but no heat exchanger or MTC manufacturing angle.

title: Swirl flow in microchannels: patterned slip walls enhance heat transport
summary: Microchannel heat sinks (MCHS) are widely used for thermal management in high-power electronics due to their ability to dissipate large heat fluxes with minimal coolant consumption. While numerous strategies - such as geometric modifications, surface disruptions, and enhanced coolant formulations - have been explored to improve heat transfer, many of these approaches increase hydraulic resistance and pumping power requirements. Recent studies have shown that slip/no-slip wall patterns can enhance flow rates and convective heat removal without additional energy input, and that patterned microstructures can induce secondary swirling motions known to promote mixing and heat transfer. Motivated by these findings, we investigate a slip/no-slip pattern specifically designed to generate swirl flow inside a straight microchannel.
